newsitem.title: SPAIN: SWIMMING-POPOV, SMITH BACK IN THE CHAMPIONSHIP FRAY.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-POPOV, SMITH BACK IN THE CHAMPIONSHIP FRAY.

text.p: Alexander Popov, victim of a knife attack last year, and fellow Olympic champion Michelle Smith are set to return to the limelight of major competition at the European swimming championships beginning on Wednesday.

The peerless Popov, who achieved unique Olympic 50 and 100 metres freestyle title doubles at the 1992 and 1996 Games, was stabbed in the abdomen by a watermelon seller in a Moscow street last August less than a month after his Atlanta triumphs.

The Australia-based Russian missed the short-course season during the northern hemisphere winter but has shown encouraging recent form and nobody appears to have the class to deny him a fourth consecutive European 100 freestyle crown and a hat-trick of 50 freestyle titles.

Smith beat the 15-year-old European short-course record for the women's 200 metres butterfly in her native Ireland last Saturday but has shunned the main international competitions since her phenomenal golden treble at the Atlanta Olympics last July.

The astonishing advances made by Smith, now 27, at such a mature competitive age after years as an also-ran gave her feats a controversial edge and raised inevitable questions of how she achieved them.
Swimming is a sport particularly sensitive to the scourge of doping but Smith has vehemently denied ever using drugs and attributes her success to improved hard training.

Smith claimed her first major long-course gold medals at the last European championships in Vienna in 1995 when she won the 200 butterfly and 200 individual medley as well as finishing second to the great Krisztina Egerszegi in the 400 individual medley.
The Irishwoman has entered the 200 and 400 individual medley and 400 freestyle -- the events she won at the Atlanta Olympics -- and the 200 butterfly and 200 and 800 freestyle.
Nobody has ever won six individual events at a meeting of this calibre and to accomplish it she would have to race -- with heats -- every day of the seven-day swimming programme.
The awesome task, which includes the finals of the hugely demanding 200 butterfly and 800 freestyle in the same session, could be within the powerful competitor's compass.
Egerszegi, one of swimming's greatest champions, was left for dead by Smith in her Olympic 400 individual medley title defence and the Hungarian has since retired.
High-profile German Franziska van Almsick, denied gold at the Atlanta Olympics, injured herself in a motorcycle accident in May and will not compete in Seville.
Van Almsick, the world 200 freestyle champion and world record holder, won six golds at the 1993 European championships and five in 1995 and would have offered Smith fierce opposition.
Fellow Germans Kerstin Kielgass, the reigning 200 freestyle champion, and Dagmar Hase, the former Olympic 400 freestyle champion, should provide her strongest freestyle challenge.

Among the men, Russian double Olympic champion Denis Pankratov should reassert his supremacy in the butterfly events having set world short-course marks for the 50, 100 and 200 events in the World Cup this year.

Pankratov failed to make the finals of the 100 and 200 butterfly at April's world short-course championships in Gothenburg but went there directly from training camps and made clear his priority was this meeting in the Olympic-sized 50-metre pool.

World 200 individual medley champion Jani Sievinen of Finland, who won three European titles in 1995 but missed gold in Atlanta, faces interesting battles with Dutchman Marcel Wouda, who took the Finn's world short-course 400 individual medley record this year, and Olympic 200 medley champion Attila Czene of Hungary.
German former world champion Jan Hoffmann, who achieved an unprecedented fourth consecutive European 1,500 freestyle title in Vienna, goes for a fifth.
The championships begin on Wednesday with diving, synchronised swimming and water polo. The long-distance races over five and 25 kms will be held in the Guadalquivir River on Friday and Sunday.
The main swimming events begin on August 19.
Water polo features with the other aquatic disciplines at the European championships for the last time. It will be held separately in Italy in 1999 when the other events will be staged in Istanbul.
